gemma4_verdict: Gemma 4 31B is a strong expert-level scientific reasoner. On GPQA Diamond (PhD-level science) it scores ~84.3% on Google's own model card (Artificial Analysis reports ~85.7%), a dramatic generational jump over Gemma 3 27B (~42%). On Humanity's Last Exam (HLE), the frontier scientific-knowledge benchmark, it scores ~22.7% (Artificial Analysis) to ~26.5% (BenchLM, June 2026) with thinking mode enabled — exceptionally high for an open-weight 31B model and far above any comparable Qwen3-32B-class model. It has a built-in 'Thinking' reasoning mode that emits 4,000+ tokens of chain-of-thought before answering, which materially boosts GPQA/HLE scores. It is natively multimodal (text + image + video-as-frames + OCR), so it can read figures, charts, and diagrams in academic papers directly — a real advantage for literature synthesis and paper critique. Weakness: relatively weaker on pure parametric factual recall (AA-Omniscience ~-45) and it is notably prone to over-refusal on medical/dual-use/sensitive research topics, which is a practical obstacle for a research assistant. Quant: GGUF Q4_K_M (~20GB) and MLX 4-bit are both readily available. [uncertain on exact HLE figure — sources span 22.7-26.5%]
qwen3_verdict: Qwen/Qwen3-32B (the May 2025 dense release, NOT the newer Qwen3.5/3.6 lines that appear in many 2026 comparison articles) is a capable scientific reasoner via its dual-mode thinking architecture. From the official Qwen3 / Qwen3-VL technical reports, Qwen3-32B in thinking mode scores GPQA Diamond 68.4, MMLU-Pro 79.1, MMLU-Redux 90.9, AIME-25 72.9, LiveBench 65.7, LiveCodeBench v6 60.6. Its GPQA Diamond of 68.4 is solid but ~16 points below Gemma 4 31B's ~84%, a meaningful gap on expert scientific reasoning. No official HLE number is published for Qwen3-32B; the much larger Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking scores only ~15.4% on HLE, so Qwen3-32B is almost certainly in the single digits to low teens — well below Gemma 4 31B. Thinking mode markedly improves its math/science/logic accuracy (it overlaps QwQ-32B on the accuracy curve) but it tends to over-generate tokens. It is TEXT-ONLY (the base 32B has no vision encoder; multimodal is the separate Qwen3-VL line), so it cannot read paper figures natively. Slightly better raw factual recall than Gemma 4 (AA-Omniscience ~-42 for the 27B-class) but still weak. Quant: GGUF Q4_K_M and MLX 4-bit widely available. [uncertain on HLE — no published Qwen3-32B figure]
benchmarks: GPQA Diamond (expert scientific reasoning): Gemma 4 31B ~84.3% (model card) / ~85.7% (Artificial Analysis) vs Qwen3-32B 68.4 (thinking, official Qwen3-VL report) — Gemma 4 leads by ~16 pts. Humanity's Last Exam (frontier science knowledge): Gemma 4 31B ~22.7-26.5% (with thinking) vs Qwen3-32B no published figure (Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking is only ~15.4%, so the 32B is likely far lower) — Gemma 4 clearly leads. MMLU-Pro: Gemma 4 31B not cleanly published in standardized form [uncertain] vs Qwen3-32B 79.1 (thinking). MMLU-Redux: Qwen3-32B 90.9. AIME 2024/2025: Gemma 4 31B 89.2% (AIME 2026, no-tools) vs Qwen3-32B 81.4 (AIME-24) / 72.9 (AIME-25). LiveCodeBench v6: Gemma 4 31B 80.0% vs Qwen3-32B 60.6. LiveBench: Qwen3-32B 65.7. BigBench Extra Hard: Gemma 4 31B 74.4%. Net: Gemma 4 wins the two dimensions the task prioritizes most (GPQA Diamond and HLE) by wide margins. [uncertain on Gemma 4 MMLU-Pro, ARC-Challenge, SciQ — not separately published]
factual_accuracy: Scientific factuality is a wash-to-slight-Qwen edge on pure recall but Gemma wins on reasoned-science accuracy. On parametric factuality (AA-Omniscience), Gemma 4 31B ~-45 vs Qwen3.5/Qwen3-class ~-42 — Qwen marginally better at avoiding short-form confabulation, though both are weak and need RAG for a research assistant. However, GPQA Diamond is itself a factuality-under-reasoning test, and there Gemma 4 (~84%) decisively beats Qwen3-32B (68.4). Both models reduce hallucination when thinking mode is ON: extended chain-of-thought, self-consistency and verification steps are well-documented to improve hard-science benchmark accuracy (the GPQA/HLE gains are themselves largely thinking-mode driven). Caveat from the literature: more sophisticated reasoning can mask remaining hallucinations more convincingly, so confident-but-wrong outputs remain a risk for both. No head-to-head SimpleQA/TruthfulQA number isolating Qwen3-32B vs Gemma 4 31B was found. [uncertain — no direct SimpleQA comparison for these exact two models, thinking-mode hallucination claim is inferential not a measured per-model delta]
inference_speed: Both run comfortably at Q4_K_M / MLX 4-bit on Apple Silicon. Qwen3-32B: ~15-24 tok/s on M4 Pro (48GB) with llama.cpp Q4_K_M, jumping to ~60 tok/s with MLX 4-bit (a known ~2.5x llama.cpp-vs-MLX gap on Qwen3). Gemma 4 31B: Q4_K_M ~20GB fits a 24GB Mac, real-time readable; MLX outperforms GGUF by 20-50%. Gemma 4 ships a dedicated draft model for speculative decoding across all sizes, which can further speed interactive agentic loops with no quality loss (Qwen3-32B has no built-in MTP draft model). For interactive research-ideation loops both are usable; Gemma 4's native speculative decoding is a modest edge. [uncertain — no Gemma 4 31B exact tok/s figure at a fixed chip; comparison drawn from M4 Pro / M5 Max community benchmarks]
multimodal_support: Gemma 4 31B: natively multimodal — text + image + video (as frames, up to ~60s at 1fps) + OCR/document parsing, with variable-aspect-ratio image handling. This lets it read paper figures, charts, tables, and diagrams directly, which is highly relevant for literature synthesis and paper critique. Qwen3-32B: TEXT-ONLY. The dense 32B has no vision encoder; Qwen's multimodal capability lives in the separate Qwen3-VL line (a different model). For a research assistant that must ingest figure-heavy PDFs, this is a decisive Gemma 4 advantage.
context_window: Gemma 4 31B: advertised 256K tokens (hybrid local-sliding + global attention, final layer always global) — easily holds many full papers (a paper is ~8k-20k tokens) for multi-paper synthesis sessions. Qwen3-32B: native 32,768 tokens, extensible to ~131,072 (128k) via YaRN RoPE scaling (validated by Qwen, supported in vLLM/SGLang/llama.cpp). So Qwen3-32B's out-of-the-box 32k is enough for 2-3 papers but needs YaRN for full literature-review sessions, and YaRN can degrade short-context quality. Effective/measured RULER-style usable context not separately published for either at these exact sizes. For the 'given these N papers, what next' use case, Gemma 4's larger native window is the safer choice. [uncertain — no published RULER effective-context score for Gemma 4 31B or Qwen3-32B specifically]
non_cuda_support: Both have strong non-CUDA support. GGUF quants (Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M, etc.) available for both via llama.cpp; both run on ROCm/AMD (llama.cpp -DGGML_HIPBLAS=ON / vLLM ROCm), Metal, MLX (Apple Silicon), and Vulkan. MLX builds for both landed quickly (Gemma 4 community MLX support 'almost immediately'). Affordable 32GB non-CUDA cards that fit a ~20GB Q4 quant: AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX (24GB — tight but workable for Q4), Radeon Pro W7800 (32GB), and Apple M-series with >=32GB unified memory (M4 Pro 48GB / M4 Max 128GB confirmed running both). Build complexity is standard llama.cpp/MLX; no exotic steps. Gemma 4's speculative-decoding draft model also works under llama.cpp. Tie on backend breadth. [uncertain — no confirmed report of a 32GB RX 9070 XT variant for either model]
over_refusal_risk: This is a real concern and slightly favors caution for BOTH, with Gemma 4 the bigger risk. Community reports (Hacker News, HuggingFace discussions) describe Gemma 4 as 'strongly censored' — it has refused legitimate medical questions and benign creative prompts; users call it 'crippled' / 'morally obstructed.' It is less censored than Gemma 3 but still over-refuses medical/biosafety/dual-use research topics, directly hitting a research-assistant use case. Counter-narrative: Qwen3/Qwen3.5 also have 'a very strong refusal rate,' described as 'unreasonably restrictive' and unsuitable for unattended batch tasks out of the box — so Qwen is NOT the clearly-permissive alternative many assume. No published XSTest scores isolate Gemma 4 31B vs Qwen3-32B. Mitigation for either: abliterated/uncensored community derivatives exist (with weaker guardrails), or careful system-prompting. Net: both pose over-refusal risk on dual-use science; Gemma 4 reportedly somewhat worse. [uncertain — no XSTest numbers for these exact two models, based on community reports]
ecosystem_toolchain: Both have mature day-one ecosystems: llama.cpp (GGUF), Ollama, MLX, vLLM, LM Studio, Unsloth all support both. Tool-call parser flags differ — Gemma 4: vLLM --tool-call-parser gemma4 (note: 'pythonic' is Gemma 3, gemma4 is correct for Gemma 4 per Labmate's own CLAUDE.md). Qwen3-32B: vLLM --tool-call-parser hermes (or qwen3 family parser) with --reasoning-parser qwen3; deployable via vllm>=0.8.5 / sglang>=0.4.6 as OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Both have thinking enabled by default in vLLM. HuggingFace model cards are high quality for both; quantized variants (FP8, NVFP4, INT4, GGUF) are plentiful, with dedicated quant comparison writeups (Kaitchup) available for Gemma 4 31B. Agentic/tool-call surface: Gemma 4 31B shows very strong agentic gains (tau2-bench Retail 86.4%); Qwen3 family is explicitly tuned for tool use. Roughly tied; both are production-ready for MCP/OpenAI tool-call format.
labmate_relevance: HIGH. Research reasoning and ideation is Labmate's core value proposition — generating novel hypotheses, designing experiments, synthesizing across papers, and finding research gaps all demand exactly the expert-level scientific reasoning (GPQA Diamond) and frontier knowledge (HLE) this dimension measures. The orchestrator brain choice here directly determines the quality of Labmate's scientific output. Multimodal paper-figure reading and large context for multi-paper synthesis are also central to the literature-review workflow, which sharpens the Gemma 4 advantage.
recommendation: Use Gemma 4 31B as Labmate's orchestrator brain for research reasoning and ideation. It wins the two benchmarks the task prioritizes most — GPQA Diamond (~84% vs 68.4) and HLE (~22-26% vs Qwen3-32B's likely single-digits/low-teens) — by wide margins, and it uniquely reads paper figures natively (Qwen3-32B is text-only) with a 256K context that comfortably holds a multi-paper synthesis session. Enable thinking mode for all hypothesis-generation and 'given these papers, what experiment next' prompts, since the GPQA/HLE gains depend on it. Two caveats that could tip a hybrid strategy: (1) Over-refusal — Gemma 4 reportedly refuses some legitimate dual-use/biosafety/medical research queries; mitigate with strong system prompts and, if needed, route sensitive-but-legitimate queries through a less-restricted model or an abliterated derivative. (2) Pure factual recall is weak in both, so wrap either model in RAG over a real paper corpus rather than trusting parametric memory. Keep Qwen3-32B as a secondary text-only reasoner only if you specifically want its slightly stronger short-form factuality or its MMLU-Pro 79.1; otherwise Gemma 4 is the clear pick for this dimension. (Note: align this on Qwen3-32B specifically — do not let newer Qwen3.5/3.6 benchmark numbers, which beat Gemma 4 on GPQA, contaminate the decision; those are different models not named in this task.)
